# FSB5 Vorbis differential fixture

`fsb5-vorbis-stereo.fsb` contains 4,800 stereo frames at 48 kHz. The source
signal is a deterministic non-silent ramp/saw pattern encoded with the system
`libvorbis 1.3.7` encoder at quality 0.4, then repacked from Ogg packets into
FSB5 packet framing. Its setup-header CRC is `0x87c121d5`.

The fixture is used only for output comparison with a separately installed
`vgmstream-cli`; the Rust implementation neither links nor redistributes
libvorbis or vgmstream. The setup packet used to reconstruct the Vorbis stream
comes from the compact, mechanically generated setup table described in
`THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md`.

`fsb5-vorbis-stereo-silence.fsb` is a minimal silent development fixture kept
for parser diagnostics; semantic output tests use the non-silent fixture.

Each `vorbis-{3..8}ch.ogg` and matching `fsb5-vorbis-{3..8}ch.fsb` pair contains
the same surround audio packets. The input is 3,840 frames of distinct integer
saw patterns, written directly as PCM16 WAVE by the Python standard library so
fixture generation does not depend on a platform's floating-point sine or
FFmpeg channel-layout remapping. `oggenc 1.4.3` with `libvorbis 1.3.7` encodes
the input at quality 4 and 32 kHz. Every channel count uses setup CRC
`0x6aad13bc`, which was already present in the checked FMOD header dictionary;
the fixtures do not add test-only setups to production. Each FSB copy removes
the three Ogg headers and keeps the setup CRC plus length-prefixed audio
packets. The ignored oracle decodes the FSB through Rust and the original Ogg
through pinned `vgmstream r2117`, then compares the complete PCM16 output.

The first six-channel comparison exposed a maximum difference of 8,396 because
Rust wrote the decoder's Vorbis speaker order directly to WAVE. After the
standard 1-8 channel Vorbis-to-WAVE permutation, every 3-8 channel layout has a
measured maximum difference of at most one. A per-channel hash also requires every
signal to remain distinct; it caught and rejected an earlier generator that
made FFmpeg remap two four-channel inputs to the same speaker.

All encoded fixtures below are regenerated by
`tools/generate_audio_fixtures.py`, which records the exact encoder invocations;
the encoders themselves are neither linked nor redistributed here.

# MPEG Layer III differential fixture

`mpeg-layer3-tone.mp3` is a 0.3-second 440 Hz tone generated with `ffmpeg`'s
`sine` source and encoded by the system `lame` at 128 kbps CBR, mono, 44.1 kHz,
with the bit reservoir and the Xing/Info tag disabled so every frame stands
alone. It is thirteen MPEG-1 Layer III frames and nothing else.

The test repacks those frames into FSB5 framing, padding each to the four-byte
boundary FSB5 requires. It replaced an all-zero fixture that compared framing
only: two readers agree on silence whatever their decoders do, so a
sample-level defect had nowhere to show.

Layer III output is not specified bit-exactly, so the tone is compared with a
one-unit tolerance; the silent cases alongside it still require exact equality.

Each `fsb5-mpeg-layer3-{3..16}ch.fsb` is a multistream counterpart. The
generator writes sixteen distinct deterministic integer triangle-wave channels,
encodes each adjacent pair as an independent stereo CBR stream, and additionally
encodes the final channel of every odd layout as mono. It disables the bit
reservoir and Xing/Info tag so every frame remains independently decodable.
Each fixture takes the required stream prefix, pads every frame to 16 bytes,
and interleaves the streams in FSB5 order for 13 frames. The set exercises odd
mono tails, the compact six/eight-channel modes, explicit channel-count metadata
for every other layout, and the verified 16-channel limit.

Distinct per-channel peaks and hashes make ordering observable rather than
merely proving that many silent channels can be written. The ignored oracle
test compares every decoded PCM sample of all fourteen fixtures with pinned
`vgmstream r2117`; the one-unit Layer III bound remains sufficient throughout.

# Opus differential fixtures

`opus-tone-packets.bin` and `opus-tone-celt-packets.bin` are 0.12-second 1 kHz
tones encoded by `ffmpeg`'s `libopus` at 24 and 64 kbps, mono, 48 kHz, in
20 ms frames. Each holds seven audio packets already in FSB5's framing -- a
little-endian `u16` length before each packet -- with the zero-length terminator
appended by the test rather than stored, so the terminator is part of what the
comparison verifies. Neither file contains the Ogg container or the OpusHead and
OpusTags packets; both streams declare the 312-sample pre-skip that FSB5
hardcodes, which the generator checks.

There are two because Opus switches between two internal codecs and this crate
decodes them to different standards. The 64 kbps stream is CELT-only and matches
`vgmstream` exactly. The 24 kbps stream is SILK/hybrid and does not: it arrives
two samples early and then differs by up to 276 against a peak near 4200. That
is a defect in `ruopus` 0.1.2 rather than in the FSB5 handling -- it reproduces
by feeding the packets straight to the decoder with no code from this crate in
the path -- and its test pins the measurement rather than accepting it.

Both replaced an all-zero fixture that compared framing only, which is how the
divergence went unnoticed: two decoders agree on silence whatever they do.

Each `opus-celt-{3..8}ch.ogg` and matching `fsb5-opus-celt-{3..8}ch.fsb`
pair contains 5,760 frames of distinct deterministic integer triangle waves at
48 kHz. The generator labels the input WAVE layout before encoding, requires
libopus mapping family 1, and checks every stream count, coupled-stream count,
and mapping byte in the authoritative `OpusHead`. This input-side check matters:
an earlier generator put `-channel_layout` on FFmpeg's output side and silently
remixed the third channel of the three-channel fixture to zero; the regular
per-channel peak and hash assertions rejected it.

Each FSB wraps the exact audio packets from its Ogg counterpart in FSB5's
little-endian length framing and declares 5,760 post-pre-skip frames. The
regular test proves that every output channel is non-silent and distinct. The
ignored oracle decodes the FSB through the Rust implementation and each
original Ogg through pinned `vgmstream r2117`, compares the complete FSB output
with the corresponding Ogg prefix, and pins the measured per-layout PCM16
deltas (the largest is nine for four channels). Because each Ogg retains its
authoritative `OpusHead`, this independently checks self-delimited multistream
packet parsing and every standard surround-to-WAVE channel order; it does not
compare the Rust decoder with another header synthesized from the same FSB
assumptions.
